node.text: # NeuralNote AI — Complete System Blueprint **Project name (codebase):** NeuralNote AI **App id:** `com.localai.notechat` **App name:** NeuralNote AI **Platform:** Android (Capacitor 8 wrapper). The iOS platform is not installed. A `server.ts` Node server exists but is legacy/dead in the packaged mobile build. **Tagline:** Offline-First Markdown Notes & Local AI Chat This document is an architecture and design blueprint derived from reading the source tree. It describes what the app is, how it is structured, and the key decisions that shape it. --- ## 1. Product Overview NeuralNote AI is a privacy-first note-taking and AI-assistant application. The core promise is **offline-first**: the user's notes and chat conversations live entirely on-device, and the AI can run locally without any network access. Cloud AI providers are supported as an optional, per-session enhancement, and all sensitive data stored at rest is encrypted. The product combines: - A full-featured **Markdown note editor** with wiki-style links, backlinks, pins, search history, a knowledge graph, tags, and focus mode. - An **AI chat** that can run either fully on-device (local Transformers.js models or native llama.cpp GGUF models with GPU offload) or against cloud providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, OpenAI-compatible endpoints). - A **RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)** pipeline that embeds the user's notes locally and lets the chat search across them. - A **tools** surface for offline summarization, proofreading, translation, YouTube summarization, and document relations. - **Google Drive backup/restore** and file export (PDF/MD/TXT/DOCX) via the Android share sheet. The single consistent thread is **local-first**: inference, embeddings, storage, and search are designed to function with zero network, with cloud as a bolt-on capability rather than a requirement. --- ## 2. Tech Stack | Concern | Technology | | --- | --- | | Mobile shell | Capacitor 8 (Android only) | | UI framework | React 19 + Vite 6 + TypeScript | | Styling | Tailwind CSS 4 (via `@tailwindcss/vite`), custom glass/aurora design system | | State management | Zustand 5 (7 domain stores) | | Animation | framer-motion, `AnimatePresence` | | Icons | lucide-react | | Persistence (browser) | IndexedDB (`neuralai-store`) + localStorage | | Encryption | AES-256-GCM (Web Crypto), device-bound key in IndexedDB | | Local LLM (in-browser) | `@huggingface/transformers` v4 in a Web Worker, WebGPU → WASM, q4 quantization | | Local LLM (native) | `llama-cpp-capacitor` (JNI) with Vulkan GPU offload | | Embeddings / RAG | MiniLM-L6-v2 (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) via Transformers.js feature-extraction, 384-dim | | Cloud AI | Direct browser fetch to Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, OpenAI-compatible endpoints | | Auth / backup | Firebase Auth (Google OAuth) + Google Drive APIs (`drive.file`/`appdata` scopes) | | File export | jsPDF (PDF), docx (DOCX), plus plain MD/TXT | | Markdown rendering | react-markdown + remark-gfm + remark-math + rehype-katex + react-syntax-highlighter | | Editor | `@uiw/react-md-editor` | | Command palette | cmdk | | Knowledge graph | react-force-graph-2d + d3-force | | Server (legacy, dead in mobile) | Express + compression + Vite middleware/static; GoogleGenAI | Build chain: `tsc --noEmit` → `vite build` → `esbuild server.ts` (bundles the Node server to `dist/server.cjs`). Tests via vitest. --- ## 3. High-Level Architecture The app is a single-page React application rendered inside a Capacitor WebView. All logic is client-side. The `server.ts` Node server is effectively dead in the packaged app (the Capacitor build ships no Node runtime; the server routes are only reachable during `npm run dev` / `npm start`). ``` +--------------------------------------------------------------+ | Android WebView | | | | React 19 SPA (src/) | | +---------------------------------------------------------+ | | | UI Layer: App / AppHeader / BottomNavigation / TabArea | | | | NotesTab | ChatsTab | ToolsTab | SettingsTab | | | +--------------------------+------------------------------+ | | | State Layer: Zustand stores + bridge hooks | | | | notesStore chatStore aiStore inferenceStore ragStore | | | | uiStore authStore syncStore | | | +--------------------------+------------------------------+ | | | Utils: db secureStorage vectorStore embeddings crypto | | | | cloudProviders fileExport googleAuth googleDrive | | | +--------------------------+------------------------------+ | | | Workers: transformerWorker (Transformers.js) | | | +--------------------------+------------------------------+ | | | Capacitor plugins: Filesystem Share FilePicker App | | | +--------------------------+------------------------------+ | | | Native: llama-cpp-capacitor (JNI + Vulkan) | | | +--------------------------+------------------------------+ | | | Storage: IndexedDB + encrypted localStorage | | +--------------------------------------------------------------+ ``` The Transformer inference runs off the main thread in a Web Worker; all heavy matrix math happens there so the UI thread stays smooth. A second, wholly native path (`llama-cpp-capacitor`) runs GGUF models through JNI into llama.cpp C++, offloading layers to the GPU (Vulkan). --- ## 4. vitest suite (29 passing baseline) ``` --- ## 5. State Management State is split across seven Zustand stores. A thin bridging layer (`src/stores/bridge.ts`) exposes **focused per-consumer hooks** built on `useShallow` so that subscribing components re-render only when the slice they consume changes, avoiding broad re-renders. A legacy `useAppBridge()` shim provides backward compatibility during migration. ### 5.1 `notesStore` Notes CRUD and content editing. - `createNewNote`, `updateNoteContent/Title`, `deleteNote` (8-second undo queue), `addTagToNote`/`removeTagFromNote`, `togglePinNote`, `toggleMarkdownCheckbox`. - Persists via encrypted `secureSet('neural_notes_v1')`; sync fallback `loadNotesSync`; async `hydrateFromDisk`. ### 5.2 `chatStore` Chat sessions + message sending orchestration. - `createNewChatSession` seeds a system message ("Ready. Model: … Backend: … 100% offline." or a cloud variant). - `deleteChatSession`, `deleteMessage`, `retryMessage` (finds the preceding user message, trims, resends with `isRetry: true`). - `sendChatMessage` is the central orchestrator: YouTube URL detection, RAG context injection, direct cloud path, or local streaming (Transformers worker / llama.cpp). - `exportChatSession` (JSON download). - Holds `CLOUD_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_PROVIDER` and per-family ceilings (see §9). ### 5.3 `aiStore` AI tool actions and cloud chat helper. - `runNoteSummarizer`, `runNoteProofreader`, `runNoteTranslator` (default target "Spanish"). - `runOnlineYoutubeSummarizer`, `runOfflineYoutubeSummarizer`, `runYoutubeSummarizerWithFallback`. - `fetchYouTubeTranscript` (timedtext + 3 Invidious instances as relay). - `runCloudChat` helper. ### 5.4 `inferenceStore` Local model lifecycle and NPU configuration. - `npuConfig` (device, model, quantization, context window, temperature, topP/topK, repetition penalty, max output tokens, power mode, custom GGUF name/size, system prompt, chat template, cloud provider/api key/model/base URL, streaming flag). Persisted debounced (400 ms) and encrypted to `neural_npu_config_v1`. - Model download/delete/load; `loadGgufFromPath` (native plugin, remembers last path in `neural_last_gguf_path_v1`). - Live tokens-per-second reporting, engine status, `hydrateFromDisk`. ### 5.5 `ragStore` RAG index coordination. - `ragEnabled`, `isIndexReady`, `indexProgress`, `buildIndex(notes)`, `searchNotes(query, topK=5)`, `loadFromDisk`, `suggestConnections` (via vector store `findRelatedNotes`). ### 5.6 `uiStore` Transient UI state: `activeTab` (`notes` | `chats` | `settings` | `tools`), show flags for keyboard-shortcuts modal, command palette, knowledge graph; `isFocusMode`; toasts. (The rendering components read live values via `UIContext`, which owns the same tab/overlay state used by the Android back button.) ### 5.7 `authStore` / `syncStore` - `authStore`: Firebase user, `handleGoogleLogin/Logout`, `initAuthListener`, `getAccessToken`. - `syncStore`: sync/restore status (`idle`|`syncing`|`success`|`error`), sync/restore log, `lastSyncTime`. ### 5.8 Bridge hooks `useAppNotes`, `useAppChat`, `useAppTools`, `useAppShell` each subscribe to only the fields they need via `useShallow`, plus the legacy `useAppBridge()`. This is deliberate: it prevents the `chatStore`/`notesStore` from spamming all consumers on every keystroke. --- ## 6. Persistence Layer ### 6.1 IndexedDB (`neuralai-store`, DB_VERSION 1) The authoritative data store. Object stores: - `notes` — notes table - `chatSessions` — chat sessions + messages - `searchHistory` — note search history - `kv` — key/value (settings, the RAG vector index `rag_vector_index`, misc) ### 6.2 Encrypted localStorage Sensitive state (notes snapshot, NPU config) is written to localStorage via `secureStorage.ts`: values are AES-256-GCM encrypted with a **device-bound key stored in IndexedDB**, so the ciphertext is useless if copied off-device. `secureGet` transparently handles missing / encrypted / legacy-plaintext entries. A **dual-write** to both IndexedDB and localStorage exists during a migration window so data survives while both paths are reconciled. ### 6.3 Hydration / startup `AppProviders` initializes the Firebase auth listener, hydrates all stores from disk (IndexedDB → encrypted localStorage), and rebuilds the RAG index when notes change (debounced 800 ms, guarded by a `hydratedRef` to avoid clobbering freshly loaded data with a stale pre-hydration rebuild). --- ## 7. On-Device AI Inference There are two independent local engines. ### 7.1 Transformers.js (in-browser, Web Worker) - Runs in `transformerWorker.ts` behind a main-thread proxy (`transformerProxy.ts`). - Loads `text-generation` pipelines from the HuggingFace Hub at `q4` quantization. - Tries **WebGPU first**, falls back to **WASM** on failure (e.g., unsupported ONNX ops); detects GPU adapter and requests FP16 features opportunistically. - Downloads are cached in IndexedDB (`hf.co_models`), with progress + stall detection, and a `loadModelLock` serializes concurrent loads. - Streaming: emits tokens in small batches (4 word-groups) to reduce postMessage overhead. - Chat templating: uses `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` when available, else a manual `formatPromptWithTemplate` supporting chatml / llama / llama3 / alpaca / phi / gemma / default. - Tokenize / decode / count tokens / delete model / abort supported via the worker protocol. - Maps common ONNX/OOM errors to user-friendly messages (e.g., "Not enough memory to load this model. Try a smaller model…"). ### 7.2 llama.cpp native (JNI, `llama-cpp-capacitor`) - A `LlamaCppEngine` singleton wraps the native plugin. - Detects the `LlamaCpp` plugin on `window.Capacitor.Plugins`. - `loadModel` via `initLlama`: `n_ctx` from config, `n_threads = min(4, cores)`, `n_batch: 2048`, `n_gpu_layers: 99` (Vulkan GPU offload), `use_mmap`, `use_mlock: false`. - Generation uses `formatChatPrompt` with template-specific stop strings and a `RepetitionDetector` (consecutive-word repetition detection + collapse) to keep output sane on small models. - `unloadModel`, timings logging. ### 7.3 Model catalog `src/utils/modelLoader.ts` defines `TRANSFORMER_MODEL_CATALOG` (8 GGUF models): | Model | Size class | | --- | --- | | Qwen2.5 | 0.5B / 1.5B / 3B | | Llama 3.2 | 1B / 3B | | SmolLM2 | 1.7B | | Gemma 2 | 2B | | Phi-3.5 Mini | 3.8B | | Mistral 7B | 7B | Each entry carries a chat template. (A separate legacy `MODEL_CATALOG` is deprecated/empty.) `loadGgufFromFile` parses GGUF headers; native GGUF files can be picked via a file picker and loaded by path. ### 7.4 Hardware detection `npuDetector.ts` probes available backends at first pointer-down (once), records the best device, and drives the informational "engine status" + inference log shown in the UI. Hardware detection intentionally performs no actual inference — it reports what is available so the user can pick a good model. After a delay, the app auto-loads the last-used GGUF model from its persisted path if present. --- ## 8. Cloud AI Providers Cloud inference is a **direct browser fetch** to each provider (no server proxy in the Capacitor build). Providers implement a common `CloudProvider` interface exposing an async generator `chat()` that yields text chunks for streaming. ### 8.1 Providers - **Gemini** — Google Generative Language API. - **OpenAI** — chat completions / responses. - **Claude** — Anthropic Messages API. - **OpenAICompatible** — generic endpoints (OpenCode / MimoCode / custom), routed by model family to the right shape: - Anthropic family → `/messages` - OpenAI "responses" family → `/responses` - otherwise → `/chat/completions` - `builtinProviders`, `getActiveProvider`, `fetchAvailableModels`, default model + base URL maps. ### 8.2 SSE streaming `parseSSEStream`, `parseAnthropicSSE`, and `parseResponsesSSE` decode server-sent events into text chunks. A **rAF-based stream flusher** batches incoming chunks and paints tokens per animation frame (smooth, consistent token rendering). A **throttled live tokens/sec reporter** feeds the streaming stats display. ### 8.3 Output-token ceilings Per-provider max output tokens prevent the app from requesting more than the provider allows and prevent silent truncation: | Provider / family | Max output tokens | | --- | --- | | Gemini | 8192 | | OpenAI | 16384 | | Claude | 64000 | | OpenCode / MimoCode | 16384 | | Custom (default) | 32768 | | Claude family | 64000 | | MiniMax | 110000 | | DeepSeek V4 Flash | 110000 | | Gemini 2.5/3 | 65536 | | DeepSeek R1 / reasoner | 65536 | | DeepSeek Chat / V3 | 8192 | | GPT-4o / Turbo | 16384 | `inferTemplateFromName` picks the correct profile from the model name. ### 8.4 Config `cloudMode.ts` decides whether cloud is available: device is `Gemini_Cloud` OR a provider + API key is configured. The user's cloud credentials (provider, API key, model, base URL, streaming) live in `npuConfig`, encrypted at rest. Keys are read client-side. --- ## 9. RAG Pipeline Retrieval-augmented generation runs entirely on-device. - **Embeddings.** `embeddings.ts` loads the `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` feature-extraction pipeline (384-dim, fp32, WASM). `chunkText` splits notes into paragraphs capped at 200 words; `stripMarkdown` removes formatting before embedding. - **Similarity.** `vectorStore.ts` stores `VectorEntry`s with embeddings **quantized from float32 to uint8 (0–255)** to shrink storage. Search dequantizes and computes **cosine similarity**, returning `topK` hits. - **Incremental indexing.** A **FNV-1a content hash** per chunk detects changes; the index re-embeds only changed chunks instead of rebuilding wholesale. The index persists to the IndexedDB `kv` store under `rag_vector_index`. - **Consumption.** On chat send (`sendChatMessage`), when RAG mode is enabled, `ragStore.searchNotes` fetches relevant chunks and injects them into the prompt as context. `suggestConnections` uses `findRelatedNotes` to surface related notes (used by the knowledge-graph / relations tooling). - **Lifecycle.** `AppProviders` deletes the cached RAG index on data-version changes and rebuilds it (debounced) when notes change, guarding against stale-context bugs that were fixed in earlier audit rounds. --- ## 10. Sync, Auth, Backup, Export ### 10.1 Google Auth `googleAuth.ts` initializes Firebase from `VITE_FIREBASE_*` env vars (gracefully no-ops if absent, so the app works without cloud). `googleSignIn` performs a popup OAuth with the `GoogleAuthProvider` extended to **Drive scopes** (`drive.file` / `appdata`) and captures the OAuth access token; `getAccessToken` returns the cached OAuth token or a refreshed Firebase ID token. ### 10.2 Google Drive backup/restore - `googleDrive.ts`: `backupToGoogleDrive` does a multipart/related upload to the app's private `appDataFolder`, create-or-PATCH (no PATCH-target filename guessing); `restoreFromGoogleDrive` pulls it back; `listBackupsOnDrive` matches files named `neural_notes_backup`. - `useDriveSync.ts` orchestrates: `performGoogleDriveBackup/Restore` with exponential-backoff retry (`withRetry`), `runRestoreFromDrive` persists restored data through all stores, and `runCloudSync` now **uploads to Drive directly** (the old `/api/sync` mock is gone). `exportBackupJSON` / `importBackupJSON` validate a `neural_note_v1_backup` version marker. ### 10.3 File export `fileExport.ts` exports chat assistant replies as PDF / MD / TXT / DOCX: - `detectExportFormat` recognizes intent phrases like "save as pdf"; `stripExportCommand` removes the export clause from the model prompt so the AI doesn't also try to answer it. - `generatePdfBase64` uses jsPDF with a custom markdown block parser (headings, code, quote, list, rule, paragraph + inline bold/italic/code). - `generateDocxBase64` uses the `docx` library. - `exportReplyAsFile` writes via the Web download API (browser) or the Capacitor Filesystem to a cache dir then hands off to the Android `Share` sheet. --- ## 11. UI Surface (Tabs) A bottom navigation switches between four tabs via an animated `TabContentArea` (`TAB_ORDER: notes → tools → chats → settings`), with framer-motion direction variants. An aurora ambient background and a glass-design system (Tailwind theme tokens like `bg-canvas`, `text-text-primary`, `glass-surface-light`) give the app its look. A custom favicon uses a teal→indigo→pink gradient. ### 11.1 NotesTab - Note explorer sidebar: search (with search history), new note, keyboard shortcuts, knowledge-graph toggle. - Editor: title, Edit/Preview toggle (`@uiw/react-md-editor` vs `MarkdownRenderer`), tags, pin. - AI selection toolbar, `DiffProposal` proofread review, `NoteChatPanel` mini-chat, backlinks/outgoing-links sidebar. ### 11.2 ChatsTab - `AutoResizeTextarea` composer, per-message **export (PDF/MD/TXT/DOCX)** and **copy** buttons, message stats (tokens, generation time). - Sidebar with Local Models management + GGUF file picker (via Capacitor file-picker + `content://` URI resolution for Xiaomi/MIUI). - RAG / General mode toggle, voice input (speech recognition), read-aloud (speech synthesis), save-reply-as-note, retry, message delete. ### 11.3 ToolsTab - NPU Co-Pilot Toolkit: summarize (offline), proofread, translate (target language select incl. Malay). - YouTube video summarizer (UI gated on cloud availability). - Document relations view (backlinks / outgoing links). ### 11.4 SettingsTab Composed of cards: Downloaded Models, Model Catalog, Chat Template, Sampler Controls, System Prompt, RAG Settings, Voice Settings, Cloud Settings, Cloud Sync status, Google Drive Backup, Local Backup Utilities. ### 11.5 Cross-cutting - **Command palette** (cmdk), **onboarding wizard**, **keyboard-shortcuts modal**, **undo toast**, **focus mode**. - **Android back button** (`App.backButton` listener): closes overlays (palette → shortcuts → focus mode → knowledge graph), then open chat → chat list, then tab → notes, then `history.back()` or `CapApp.exitApp()`. - **Global shortcuts:** Ctrl+N new note, Ctrl+F search, Ctrl+K palette, Ctrl+Shift+F focus mode, Ctrl+Shift+S sync, Escape to clear overlays. --- ## 12. Key Data Flows ### 12.1 Sending a chat message (cloud path) 1. `ChatsTab` composer → `chatStore.sendChatMessage`. 2. Detect YouTube URL; if present and cloud is configured, route through the YouTube summarizer. 3. If RAG enabled, call `ragStore.searchNotes(query)` and inject relevant note chunks as context. 4. Create the user message; if streaming, create a stream-flusher + live tokens/sec reporter. 5. `getActiveProvider().chat(...)` → SSE parse → flusher paints tokens per rAF frame → append assistant message. 6. Persist the session; record `tokensUsed` and `generationTimeMs`. ### 12.2 Sending a chat message (local path) 1. Same entry (`sendChatMessage`). 2. Branch on active backend: `TransformersEngine` (HTML5 GPU) or `LlamaCppEngine` (native). 3. Build the prompt: system prompt + (RAG context) + conversation history via the model's chat template. 4. Stream tokens back (worker batches / llama native), run through `RepetitionDetector`, flush to the UI, persist. ### 12.3 Loading a local model 1. User picks a catalog model or a GGUF file (file picker → content:// URI). 2. `inferenceStore.loadGgufFromPath` (native) or `transformerProxy.loadModel` (worker). 3. Progress events flow: download progress (percent + status) → pipeline dispose of prior model → load (WebGPU try → WASM fallback) → tokenizer load (best effort) → status `ready`. 4. The last GGUF path persists (`neural_last_gguf_path_v1`) and auto-loads on next launch. ### 12.4 RAG build / search 1. On notes change, `AppProviders` debounces 800 ms → `ragStore.buildIndex`. 2. `vectorStore.buildIndex` hashes each chunk (FNV-1a), re-embeds changed chunks, quantizes to uint8, persists to `kv.rag_vector_index`. 3. On query, `searchIndex` dequantizes, cosine-compares, returns top-K chunks. ### 12.5 Drive backup 1. `performGoogleDriveBackup` → `getAccessToken` → `backupToGoogleDrive` (multipart upload to appDataFolder, create-or-PATCH, retry with backoff). 2. Restore reverses: list backups, fetch, validate version, `runRestoreFromDrive` persists through all stores. --- ## 13. Security & Privacy Model - **Local-first:** notes, chats, embeddings, and models live on-device. No telemetry server. - **Encryption at rest:** sensitive localStorage values AES-256-GCM encrypted, key is device-bound in IndexedDB. - **Cloud keys are client-side** and optional; no cloud provider is contacted unless the user configures one and sends a message. - **CSP** (`index.html`) restricts connect-src to known AI providers, Firebase/Google, HuggingFace (model downloads), YouTube, and WebSockets; frame-src allows YouTube embeds. - **Honest fallbacks:** when a cloud feature is unavailable (e.g., offline YouTube transcription), the app degrades to the local model or a clear message rather than silently claiming success. - **Diagnostics toggles** (cleartext, `webContentsDebuggingEnabled`) are enabled only when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`. --- ## 14. Build & Deploy ### 14.1 Development - `npm run dev` → `tsx server.ts` serves the SPA via Vite middleware on the local Node server (also exposes the legacy `/api/*` routes for browser-only development). - Tests: `npm test` (vitest), `npm run test:coverage`. ### 14.2 Production build ``` tsc --noEmit && vite build && esbuild server.ts ... --outfile=dist/server.cjs ``` Output: static SPA in `dist/` + bundled server. Postinstall runs `scripts/patch-plugin.cjs` to patch a Capacitor plugin. ### 14.3 Android (the shipped target) - `npx cap sync android` copies `dist/` into `android/app/src/main/assets/public/`, including `server.cjs` (present but inert in the WebView build). - `androidScheme: 'https'`, `CapacitorHttp.enabled: true` (lets the SPA issue cross-origin requests to AI providers / Google / HuggingFace). - APK built and deployed to physical devices (Xiaomi MIUI) via `adb` in the standard workflow. ### 14.4 Known architectural caveats - The `server.ts` `/api/*` routes (`/api/chat`, `/api/summarize`, `/api/proofread`, `/api/translate`, `/api/youtube-summarize`, `/api/sync`, `/api/health`) are **legacy/dead** in the packaged mobile app — the SPA talks to providers directly. They exist for the browser dev harness. - iOS is not configured (`@capacitor/ios` absent); Android is the only native platform. --- ## 15. Notable Design Decisions 1. **Offline-first is the load-bearing decision.** Storage, embeddings, search, and inference all run locally; cloud is additive. 2. **Two local inference paths** (browser Transformers.js + native llama.cpp) give the user both an install-free option and a fast Vulkan-accelerated option. 3. **Focused store selectors** (`bridge.ts` + `useShallow`) avoid the classic Zustand broad-re-render problem. 4. **Encrypted, device-bound storage** treats on-device data as sensitive by default. 5. **Dual-write during migration** keeps data available while storage layers are reconciled. 6. **Per-provider output-token ceilings** prevent hard truncation bugs that earlier rounds discovered independently per provider. 7. **Incremental RAG index** (FNV-1a hashing) avoids rebuilding embeddings for unchanged notes. 8. **Template-aware chat formatting** (apply_chat_template with a manual fallback per model family) keeps local chat correct across very different model tokenizers. 9. **WebGPU→WASM fallback** with friendly error translation keeps model loading robust across heterogeneous Android GPUs. 10. **Direct cloud fetch with client-side keys** fits a client-only Capacitor deployment (no confidential keys can ever be embedded in a shipped app).

# BullshitBench v2 A benchmark that tests whether AI models **push back on nonsense instead of confidently answering it**. Created by Peter Gostev (of arena.ai); v2 is already out despite the benchmark being new. ## Core idea Presents models with "bullshit" — prompts that are *grammatically and syntactically correct but have no actual meaning* — plus plausible-but-false claims across real domains. A good model should recognize the problem and say so, rather than confidently generating an incorrect answer. ## What it tests - **Challenge vs. compliance** — Does the model refuse to answer a nonsensical prompt, or hallucinate a confident-sounding answer? - **Real-world domains** — v2 covers coding, medical, legal, finance, and physics prompts (per Adam Holter's write-up) - **Plausible falsehoods** — Prompts that look reasonable on the surface but are logically flawed or factually wrong ## Key results (v2) - **Claude and Qwen are the standout families** — the only ones that reliably push back against plausible-but-false prompts - **Most models still fail** — general sentiment: "most models still can't smell BS" even on v2 ## Relevance to my projects This is directly relevant to my RAG/agent work: - My "RAG System Prompt" note already encodes the same principle: *"If retrieved notes have low relevance, acknowledge this limitation"* - A model's BullshitBench score is a proxy for whether it will: - Say "I don't have enough context" instead of making things up - Flag contradictory or nonsensical user input - Acknowledge when retrieved documents are weak or irrelevant **Takeaway:** For agent stacks, this benchmark may matter *more* than raw coding benchmarks — it's about trustworthiness in production.
